paragraphs.english: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
paragraphs.chinese: 越来越多美国人选择在达到退休年龄后继续工作很长时间，这一日益明显的趋势可能颠覆旧有的劳动力模式。

paragraphs.english: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade. Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees’—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
paragraphs.chinese: 哈里斯民意调查机构为德美利证券开展的一项调查显示，每三名至少40岁的美国人中，就有一人已经在退休后工作，或计划这样做，以应对更长的寿命。更令人惊讶的是，调查发现，超过一半的“不退休者”——也就是打算退休后继续工作，或退休后又重返岗位的人——表示，即使有足够的钱安享晚年，他们仍会在年老时工作。

paragraphs.english: Financial needs aren’t the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend. Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression. About 72% of “unretiree” respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
paragraphs.chinese: 经济需要并不是“不退休”趋势的唯一原因。根据这项研究，其他原因还包括个人充实感，例如保持思维敏锐、防止无聊或避免抑郁。约72%的“不退休者”受访者表示，他们会在退休后重返工作岗位，以保持头脑活跃；59%的人则说，这与维持生计有关。

paragraphs.english: “The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade. “It’s not just about finances. The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”
paragraphs.chinese: 德美利证券退休业务高级经理克里斯廷·拉塞尔说：“退休的概念正在变化。这不仅仅是财务问题。工作的价值也在推动人们过了退休年龄后继续工作。”

paragraphs.english: One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer. The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 32% from the prior year, according to the US. Census Bureau. That’s also up 302% since 2010. Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the US. workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations. The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades. About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
paragraphs.chinese: 退休模式发生变化的原因之一，是美国人的寿命延长了。根据美国人口普查局的数据，2018年，65岁及以上人口占总人口的16%，比前一年增长32%，比2010年增长302%。美国老年人也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体，而且婴儿潮一代的预期寿命将长于前几代人。过去三十年间，达到退休年龄的人参与劳动的比例翻了一番。资产管理公司United Income的数据显示，2月份，65岁及以上人群中约有20%仍在工作，而1985年1月这一比例曾降至历史低点10%。

paragraphs.english: Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2000 adults between 40 to 79. Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life, according to the survey. Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
paragraphs.chinese: 德美利证券这项针对2000名40至79岁成年人开展的研究显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄，以保住自己的养老积蓄。调查显示，十名“不退休者”中有六名正在为更长的寿命增加储蓄。该公司表示，最常见的做法包括减少总体开支、购买人寿保险，以及尽可能提高向退休账户缴存的金额。

paragraphs.english: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth. He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
paragraphs.chinese: 总部位于巴尔的摩的财务规划公司Facet Wealth联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多选择退休后继续工作的人，之所以作这样的准备，是因为担心晚年难以维持生计。他建议，临近退休的人应当与财务顾问沟通，设定长期财务目标。

paragraphs.english: “The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said. “It’s not just a financial decision, but an emotional one. Many people believe they can’t retire”
paragraphs.chinese: 韦斯说：“人生最具挑战的时刻，是结婚、组建家庭，以及最终退休。这不仅是一项财务决定，也是一项情感决定。很多人觉得自己退不了休。”

sentenceNotes.sentence: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: One in three Americans have or plan to have a job.
sentenceNotes.structure: who从句限定Americans的年龄；to prepare表示目的；according to引出来源，conducted过去分词短语修饰survey。
sentenceNotes.translation: 哈里斯民意调查机构为德美利证券开展的一项调查显示，每三名至少40岁的美国人中，就有一人已经在退休后工作，或计划这样做，以应对更长的寿命。
sentenceNotes.tip: 先确认比例的统计对象是“至少40岁的美国人”，不是全部美国人。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: many people ... are preparing to do so.
sentenceNotes.structure: who从句修饰people，because解释继续工作的原因；said Brent Weiss是后置报道语；a co-founder为姓名的同位语，说明身份。
sentenceNotes.translation: Facet Wealth联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多选择退休后继续工作的人，之所以作这样的准备，是因为担心晚年难以维持生计。
